Subject: Production impact - 2027-04-12 07:14-07:48 PT (possible SLA)

Hi Rishi —

We saw a service-wide 503 spike affecting our ingestion endpoints on Apr 12 between ~07:14 and 07:48 PT. Our telemetry shows increased error rate and elevated latencies for ~34 minutes. Can you confirm the impacted window on your side and advise whether Cloudworks is eligible for an SLA adjustment/compensation? We need the official downtime window, a short rationale, and any evidence you can share (logs or timeline) for our procurement/audit team.

Attaching a summary from our side (ops-digest-20270412.pdf). Let me know if you need more.

Thanks,
Lina

Hi Lina —

Thanks for the heads up and for the ops digest. We are investigating now. Initial SRE telemetry shows an elevated 5xx window beginning at 07:12 PT and back to baseline at ~07:50 PT for your tenant. We will need:

- Any client-side timestamps you can share (helps correlate request IDs)

Ill loop in Monica and Marissa to coordinate the formal verification and compensation flow. Monica: can you pull the tenant-specific service logs and the preliminary incident timeline? Marissa: if eligible, well follow the SLA remediation process and prepare a credit memo for procurement.

Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:40:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Production impact - 2027-04-12 07:14-07:48 PT (possible SLA)

Rishi / Marissa —

I pulled the tenant logs and validated request-id traces for Cloudworks. Summary:
- Error spike (5xx) between 07:11:58 and 07:50:12 PT for their tenant-specific router.
- Root cause appears to be a misrouted batch job that exhausted a subset of serving shards; router returned 503s due to backpressure.
- Affected requests: 22,431 unique request IDs (per tenant filter).

I attached two artifacts: incident-timeline-20270412.csv and service-logs-20270412.tar.gz. The SRE timeline includes event markers for autoscale attempts and the rollback that resolved the condition.

Prelim SLO calculation: availability drop exceeded the 99.95% threshold for ~34 minutes; this meets the criteria for an SLA adjudication. I'll hand off the formal assessment to Marissa for compensation calculation.

Monica
Monica Patel
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Next steps: SLA adjudication & credit routing for Cloudworks

Hi all —

Thanks Monica for the analysis and Lina for flagging. Summary of proposed next steps:
1) Confirm the official impacted window: 2027-04-12T07:11:58-2027-04-12T07:50:12 PT (converted to UTC in the attached timeline).
2) Prepare an SLA adjudication memo for Cloudworks procurement outlining the eligible credit and rationale.
3) Issue a one-time usage credit applied to the Apr invoice; if Cloudworks prefers a different remediation (e.g., service credit schedule), we can discuss.

Immediate asks for Cloudworks: please reply to confirm you accept the attached incident window and whether you prefer a credit on next invoice or a scheduled service credit.

I am attaching the SLO evaluation PDF (slo-eval-summary-20270412.pdf) and the SRE artifacts. Ill open HubSpot ticket RW-ACCT-5421 and create the credit memo draft for your review.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
